Soil

Fine Dining · Pangrati
★ 4.8 1465 reviews €€€€ 1.6 mi · 5 min from Syntagma

Tasos Mantis cooks out of a two-storey 1925 neoclassical house in Pangrati - wooden floors, high ceilings, an open kitchen and a chef's counter on the ground floor, and a walled garden that is one of the loveliest summer rooms in Athens. Much of what lands on the plate comes from his own garden at Alepochori, which earned Soil a Michelin Green Star alongside its star. A single tasting menu, fourteen courses, and a wine list with real conviction.

72 days dry aged beef · Amberjack, pear, loquat, lovage · Grouper, kombu beurre blanc · Shrimp, orange, mussels, marigold
Two to four weeks ahead; the garden and the chef's counter go first.

Sushimou

Fine Dining · Syntagma
★ 4.8 1121 reviews €€€ 0.5 mi · 2 min from Syntagma

Ten or so seats around a pale wooden counter, one chef, one menu, and absolutely no negotiation: raw fish and rice, sashimi and nigiri, nothing cooked, no rolls. Darren Chin-trained Antonis Drakoularakos sources Greek fish and treats it with Edomae discipline, and the whole thing runs at €58 a head - the best value fine dining in Athens by some margin. Parties are capped at four; the room is the antithesis of a scene.

Omakase of sashimi and nigiri, Greek fish only
Phone only, after 14:00, and often two to three weeks out; maximum four guests.

  • Omakase set menu — Sashimi and nigiri only; no rolls, no cooked or vegan options €58 per person

CTC Urban Gastronomy

Fine Dining · Psyrri

Alexandros Tsiotinis runs one of the most quietly confident rooms in the city on a workaday Kerameikos street - dark, low and deliberately anonymous from outside, all warm wood and focused light within. There is no choosing: the eleven-stage CTC Voyage arrives blind, each course engineered to set up the next. It is the Athens tasting menu for people who want to be surprised rather than reassured.

Tudor Hall

Fine Dining · Syntagma
★ 4.6 1100 reviews €€€€ 0.2 mi · 1 min from Syntagma

Seventh floor of the King George, with a wood-panelled Tudor-revival room on one side and a veranda staring straight at the Parthenon on the other - it is arguably the single best restaurant view in Athens. Nikos Livadias cooks with real precision: langoustine two ways, Dover sole with Aegina pistachio, wagyu with tosazu. The degustation at €165 is the city's most polished hotel dining experience, and the bar lounge stays open late.

Langoustine grilled and tartare · Dover sole with Aegina pistachio · Wagyu beef sirloin, tosazu · Warm chocolate souffle
Two to three weeks ahead for a veranda table at sunset.

Varoulko Seaside

Fine Dining · Piraeus
★ 4.6 5142 reviews €€€€ 6.3 mi · 13 min from Syntagma

Lefteris Lazarou was the first Greek chef to win a Michelin star, and Varoulko - opened in 1987 as the city's first exclusively seafood fine-dining room - remains his stage. The seaside incarnation sits right on the Mikrolimano marina in Piraeus, white and blue and open to the masts, which is exactly the right frame for octopus carpaccio and cuttlefish risotto. A long lunch here, with the boats knocking, is one of the great Athenian pleasures.

Octopus carpaccio with smoked fava · Cuttlefish risotto · Red mullet with cauliflower textures · Fish soup with grouper
One to two weeks ahead; waterside tables at sunset go earliest.

Materia Prima

Fine Dining · Koukaki
★ 4.6 840 reviews €€€ 1.4 mi · 4 min from Syntagma

The Koukaki original is a small, warm, wood-and-glass bistro with five hundred labels on the list and a cheese counter that Athenians treat as a destination in itself. The kitchen keeps things seasonal and Mediterranean - built to partner the bottle rather than upstage it - and the staff will happily talk you through Greek indigenous varieties for an hour. It is the neighbourhood wine bar every city wishes it had.

Seasonal Mediterranean small plates · Greek cheese selection · 500-label wine list
A few days ahead; the room is small and locals book it.

Spondi

Fine Dining · Pangrati
★ 4.5 1432 reviews €€€€ 1.6 mi · 5 min from Syntagma

Continuously awarded by Michelin since 2002, Spondi is the grande dame of Athenian fine dining and still the most romantic table in Pangrati: a vaulted stone cellar and a bougainvillea-hung courtyard in a converted nineteenth-century house. The kitchen works in a refined French idiom - foie gras, turbot, sweetbreads - with Greek produce doing the talking underneath. Come for the Discovery menu and let the sommelier drive.

Foie gras parfait · Turbot · Pan-fried foie gras · Sweetbread · Chocolate dessert
Two to three weeks ahead for a Friday or Saturday courtyard table; midweek is easier.

The Zillers Rooftop Gastronomy

Fine Dining · Syntagma
★ 4.5 2600 reviews €€€€ 0.5 mi · 2 min from Syntagma

The most photogenic star in Athens: a narrow rooftop above a neoclassical boutique hotel on Mitropoleos, with the Acropolis floodlit and close enough to feel theatrical. Executive chef Vassilis Roussos runs two tasting menus, Synecdoche and Synthesis, that read as a modern Greek argument rather than a hotel dining room. Ask for a rail table at sunset and let the evening do the rest.

Nolan

Fine Dining · Syntagma
★ 4.5 4529 reviews €€€ 0.4 mi · 2 min from Syntagma

Sotiris Kontizas' small, sharply designed room on Voulis is the place that taught Athens to eat Greek and Asian in the same mouthful, and a decade on it is still the city's most reliable weeknight booking. The menu is a single column of short, precise plates - lentils with lakerda and kasseri, beef cheek with anchovy and black truffle - priced so you can order widely. Grey walls, warm wood, a room that never shouts.

Birdman

Fine Dining · Syntagma
★ 4.5 33 reviews €€€ 0.4 mi · 2 min from Syntagma

Thirty-five seats, a robata grill, a wall of records and no interest whatsoever in ceremony - Birdman is the Athens room that made yakitori a serious proposition. Chicken is worked neck-to-tail onto skewers, wagyu nigiri changes daily, and the dry-aged yakiniku cuts land with jalapeno salsa and tomato ponzu. Natural wine, Japanese whisky, vinyl on the deck: the most fun you can have at this level of cooking.

Chef's selection wagyu nigiri · Tsukune with spicy miso and shiso · Japanese Wagyu A5 sando · Udon carbonara
Book a week or two ahead; the counter is the seat to ask for.

Vezene

Ari Vezene's bistro behind the Hilton is where Athens goes when it wants fire and protein handled properly - a wood-burning kitchen, dry-aged beef, whole fish, and a cote de boeuf that arrives like an event. Delta Restaurant

Fine Dining · Faliro
★ 4.4 692 reviews €€€€ 3.9 mi · 8 min from Syntagma

Athens' only two-star kitchen sits on the fifth floor of the Greek National Opera inside Renzo Piano's Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center, a long pale room of glass and quiet oak that looks out over the Saronic Gulf. Giorgos Papazacharias and Thanos Feskos build a twelve-stage menu almost entirely from the restaurant's own farm and a tight circle of Greek growers, which is why the Guide also handed it a Green Star. It is the most serious, most composed evening in the city, and it feels less like a restaurant than a cultural institution that happens to cook.

12 Stages tasting menu · farm vegetables from the Delta garden · Greek terroir wine flights
Book three to six weeks ahead for a weekend; a €100 per-reservation deposit is taken at booking.

Hytra

Fine Dining · Koukaki
★ 4.4 2177 reviews €€€€ 1.8 mi · 5 min from Syntagma

Perched on top of the Onassis Stegi cultural centre, Hytra is a sleek grey-and-glass room with a rooftop bar that looks straight down Syngrou to the sea. Chef Yiorgos Felemengas takes traditional Greek recipes apart and rebuilds them with real technical polish - bourdeto, fricassee, Cretan sour milk - across three degustation menus and a tight a la carte. It is the dressiest of the city's star kitchens and the easiest to combine with a concert downstairs.

Papadakis

Fine Dining · Kolonaki
★ 4.4 984 reviews €€€ 0.9 mi · 3 min from Syntagma

Argiro Barbarigou brought her Paros cooking to a pale, calm corner of Kolonaki and turned it into the city's most elegant seafood address - white walls, blue accents, a room that reads as an island house transposed to the smartest street in Athens. The kitchen is quietly technical: sea bass ceviche, chickpeas cooked fifteen hours over charcoal, grouper with fresh truffle. Lunch here on a Saturday is a very Athenian pleasure.

ERGON House

Fine Dining · Syntagma
★ 4.3 6662 reviews €€€ 0.4 mi · 2 min from Syntagma

A hotel built around a food market, or a food market that happens to have bedrooms above it - either way, ERGON House is one of the most beautifully executed interiors in central Athens, all terrazzo, brass, glasshouse roof and stacked Greek produce. The kitchen cooks from the counters around it: wood-oven peinirli, aged Greek cuts, whole fish chosen at the ice. It runs from nine in the morning to one at night, which makes it the most useful smart address in the centre.

A 1900s mansion with a courtyard garden strung with lights - Balthazar has been the city's most reliably glamorous night out for decades, and it still fills every table in summer. A restored neoclassical mansion in Metaxourgeio with a courtyard garden that feels like a secret - candlelight, olive trees, and a room that has been quietly setting the standard for Athenian fine dining for two decades. Kuzina

Fine Dining · Psyrri
€€€ 0.9 mi · 3 min from Syntagma

Aris Tsanaklidis' long-running room on the pedestrianised stretch of Adrianou has one asset nothing else can match: a roof terrace with the Acropolis directly overhead and the Ancient Agora at your feet. Downstairs is a warm, art-hung dining room with an open kitchen; upstairs, from April to October, is where the evening should happen. The cooking is playful modern Greek with an international accent, and it holds its own against the view.

Modern Greek plates from the seasonal menu
A week or more for a terrace table in summer; ask specifically for the Tarazza.

Daphne Valente pleats everything - dresses, tunics, scarves, even her bags - into sculptural pieces that fold to nothing and shake out uncreased, which makes them the most practical beautiful thing you can buy in Athens. The komboloi taken entirely seriously: several hundred strands strung from Baltic and Latin American amber, faturan, coral, yusuri, ebony, horn and semi-precious stone, displayed like fine jewellery because that is what the good ones are. A small, sharply priced shop attached to one of the city's better private art foundations, where the merchandise is genuinely tied to what is on the walls - jewellery, silk scarves, coasters and sculptures produced alongside each exhibition. Combine it with a coffee on the first-floor terrace looking over Vasilissis Sofias.

Ilias Lalaounis rebuilt the lost techniques of Mycenaean and Minoan goldsmiths, and the museum he left behind on the Acropolis's south slope keeps his private atelier intact. Ateliers & Makers · Vyronas
Not published — online ordering, prices on the site 2.4 mi · 7 min from Syntagma

Roughly two hundred years of unbroken family practice sit behind Elpida Kourtzi's wheel, and the work carries that weight lightly — bracelets and rings in fired clay alongside tableware and older vintage forms. They take commissions for wedding and baptism favours, which is the most Greek possible way to be handed an object. Vyronas is out of the centre, but this is a genuine workshop, not a showroom.

Ceramic bracelets, earrings, necklaces and rings · tableware · vintage pottery forms · commissioned favours (bomboniera)
Contact ahead to visit the workshop; pottery workshops can be booked through the site.

Pipinas Coppersmith Workshop

Ateliers & Makers · Psyrri
Not published — priced in the shop 1.1 mi · 5 min from Syntagma

Stamatis and Manolis Pipinas have been beating copper on Navarchou Apostoli for thirty-five years, among the last of a Psyrri trade that once filled the street. Everything is raised and finished by hand — the briki for Greek coffee is the obvious buy and the best one, small enough for hand luggage and useful every morning for the rest of your life. Go in the morning, when the hammering is going.

Briki (Greek coffee pot) · copper wine carafe · hand-raised trays · ornamental copper pieces
No appointment — walk in during working hours.
Map +30 210 523 1477

Dimitris Koutsipetsidis — Bookbinding Corner

Ateliers & Makers · Athens (address on request)
Commission-based — quoted per book

Dimitris Koutsipetsidis fell into bookbinding at a book fair, abandoned linguistics for it, and has been sewing, paring and tooling by hand since 2010 — making some of his own tools along the way. He works in leather, fabric and copper, and takes commissions: bring a text that matters and he will give it a body worth keeping. He has taught since 2013, so a seminar is a genuine option rather than a courtesy.

Commissioned full-leather binding · longstitch leather journal · rebinding of a family book · a place on a bookbinding seminar
By appointment only; address given on request. Seminars listed on his site.

Athens Loom Weaving Workshop

Ateliers & Makers · Makrygianni (Acropolis)
€95 per person 1.3 mi · 4 min from Syntagma

Two hours at a traditional loom in the shadow of the Acropolis, with an instructor who lets you choose what you are making before you start — coasters, a placemat, a clutch, a small tapestry on its own frame. Weaving is the one craft where you can watch the object accumulate thread by thread, which is exactly why it makes such a good gift. Sessions are small and run three times a week.

Set of four woven coasters · 45×30cm placemat · woven clutch/pouch · 50×30cm scatter rug · hand-woven bracelet · small tapestry on a portable frame
Book online in advance; Tuesdays 11:00, Thursdays and Saturdays 18:30. Full refund if cancelled 24 hours ahead.
